nodes.name: Afghanistan
nodes.note: White Islamic Emirate flag used by the de facto authorities since 2021. The former republic’s tricolour remains in use by opponents and some overseas representations.
nodes.imageCredit: Zoltan Horvath / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Burkina Faso
nodes.note: Adopted in 1984 under Thomas Sankara. Red represents revolutionary struggle, green agriculture and hope, and the yellow star the guidance of the revolution. Comparisons with Viet Cong and MPLA flags are proposed in vexillological commentary.

nodes.name: DR Congo
nodes.note: The blue field and gold star derive from Congo’s nineteenth-century flag, predating the United Nations. The current diagonal design was adopted in 2006.

nodes.name: Cuba
nodes.note: Designed for the nineteenth-century independence movement and first flown in 1850; adopted nationally in 1902.

nodes.name: Cabo Verde
nodes.note: Adopted in 1992. Pedro Gregório Lopes explained the blue through the sea and sky and the ten-star circle through the islands and dialogue. He explicitly rejected claims that the resemblance established an EU model.

nodes.name: Denmark
nodes.note: The Dannebrog is attested in the medieval period. The account of a flag falling from the sky in 1219 is a later legend.

nodes.name: Guyana
nodes.note: Whitney Smith’s original proposal was revised before adoption in 1966: red and green were reversed and black and white borders added. Sources disagree over attribution of the revisions. Flag-family surveys classify its palette as Pan-African; Smith’s explanation gives national and indigenous meanings.

nodes.name: Haiti
nodes.note: The republican blue-red tradition was restored in 1986 after the Duvalier black-red flag. The coat of arms identifies the state version.

nodes.name: Hungary
nodes.note: The red-white-green tricolour dates to 1848. The plain national flag was restored in 1957 after removal of the communist emblem.

nodes.name: Kenya
nodes.note: The independence flag retained KANU’s black-red-green stripes, adding narrow white separators and a Maasai shield with crossed spears. KANU continued the earlier KAU party colours, within the wider Garvey colour tradition.

nodes.name: Libya
nodes.note: The 1951 independence flag was restored during the 2011 revolution. Its central black band preserves the Senussi/Cyrenaican emblem. The palette follows Libyan regional and dynastic symbolism.

nodes.name: Malawi
nodes.note: The 1964 rising-sun design was restored in May 2012 after the two-year full-sun redesign.

nodes.name: Malaysia
nodes.note: Developed from the Federation of Malaya flag of 1950. Fourteen stripes and star points represent the federation. Proposed Majapahit ancestry remains uncertain.

nodes.name: Poland
nodes.note: The ordinary white-red national flag continued through the Polish People’s Republic and after 1989; state-emblem variants differed.

nodes.name: Portugal
nodes.note: Red and green were the colours of Portuguese republican movements before the 1910 revolution.

nodes.name: Romania
nodes.note: The vertical blue-yellow-red arrangement dates to 1866. The current plain flag was restored in December 1989 after removal of the communist emblem.

nodes.name: Singapore
nodes.note: Designed in 1959 under Toh Chin Chye. The committee considered Indonesia’s red-over-white flag while choosing a distinct Singaporean design. The crescent and five stars carry Singapore’s national ideals.

nodes.name: South Sudan
nodes.note: The national flag continues the SPLM design. Blue signifies the Nile, while the yellow star has been explained as unity or a guiding light. A specific Kenyan model remains uncertain.

nodes.name: Syria
nodes.note: Green-white-black with three red stars, based on Syria’s earlier independence flag. Used by the new authorities from December 2024 and constitutionally adopted in March 2025; minor proportional differences are collapsed.

nodes.name: Eswatini
nodes.note: The Swazi shield, spears and fighting staff express protection and national heritage. Kenya uses a distinct Maasai shield and spears within the same broad emblem tradition.

nodes.name: Venezuela
nodes.note: Venezuela retained the Miranda/Gran Colombian tricolour after separating in 1830. Later changes to the stars are consolidated.

nodes.name: Taiwan
nodes.note: Taiwan: self-governing; sovereignty disputed.

nodes.name: Kosovo
nodes.note: Kosovo: partially recognised state.

nodes.name: Western Sahara
nodes.note: Flag of the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic; sovereignty over Western Sahara is disputed.

nodes.name: Cook Islands
nodes.note: Cook Islands: self-governing in free association with New Zealand.

nodes.name: Niue
nodes.note: Niue: self-governing in free association with New Zealand.

nodes.name: England
nodes.note: Constituent nation of the United Kingdom. A medieval cross tradition with no single modern adoption date.

nodes.name: Scotland
nodes.note: Constituent nation of the United Kingdom. A medieval cross tradition with no single modern adoption date.

nodes.name: Wales
nodes.note: Constituent nation of the United Kingdom.

nodes.name: Hawaii
nodes.note: The Union flag canton reflects historical British connections; eight stripes represent the principal islands.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 16 September 2006 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: United Nations
nodes.note: The UN emblem grew from the 1945 San Francisco conference badge. Early drafting substituted olive branches (peace) for laurel (victory); the map was revised in 1946 and the flag adopted in 1947.

nodes.name: Prince’s Flag
nodes.note: Orange-white-blue Dutch revolt flag. Continued as a political symbol after red-white-blue became dominant.
nodes.imageCredit: Mark Sensen / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Union Flag, 1606
nodes.note: Combined the crosses of England and Scotland; the Irish saltire was added in 1801.
nodes.imageCredit: Željko Heimer / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: St Patrick’s saltire
nodes.note: Associated with the Order of St Patrick and incorporated into the Union Flag in 1801.
nodes.imageCredit: Vincent Morley / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: British Blue Ensign
nodes.note: A maritime template for many colonial and later national flags. Still in use; 1864 marks the modern service allocation.
nodes.imageCredit: Clay Moss / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: British Red Ensign
nodes.note: A British maritime flag, here shown in its post-1801 form. Its history predates this date.
nodes.imageCredit: Martin Grieve / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Grand Union Flag
nodes.note: Thirteen stripes with the pre-1801 Union canton preceded the Stars and Stripes.
nodes.imageCredit: Rick Wyatt / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: East India Company
nodes.note: Representative pre-1801 company ensign with a Union canton. A proposed influence on the Grand Union Flag, but direct borrowing is unproven.
nodes.imageCredit: Phil Nelson / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Ethiopian plain tricolour
nodes.note: Green-yellow-red without the modern emblem; a long-used civil form. Ethiopia adopted a tricolour in 1897, but early ordering and emblems varied.
nodes.imageCredit: Ivan Sache / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: UNIA / Pan-African flag
nodes.note: Marcus Garvey’s red-black-green banner remains a flag of the Pan-African movement.
nodes.imageCredit: Rick Wyatt / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: African National Congress
nodes.note: Black-green-gold movement flag; one source of colours retained in democratic South Africa. The uncharged tricolour version is shown.
nodes.imageCredit: Jorge Candeias / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Arab Revolt
nodes.note: Black-green-white stripes with a red triangle. The revolt began in 1916; this arrangement is commonly dated to 1917.
nodes.imageCredit: Filip Van Laenen / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Arab Liberation Flag
nodes.note: Red-white-black revolutionary banner associated with Egypt’s 1952 revolution; variants carry different emblems. A plain colour-pattern version is shown.
nodes.imageCredit: Santiago Dotor / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: United Arab Republic
nodes.note: Two green stars represented Egypt and Syria. Later reused by Syria, 1980–2024.
nodes.imageCredit: Eugene Ipavec / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Syria, Assad-era flag
nodes.note: The two-star red-white-black flag was replaced after Assad’s fall. This node represents its 1980–2024 use.
nodes.imageCredit: Zoltan Horvath / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Miranda’s tricolour
nodes.note: Yellow-blue-red revolutionary colours introduced by Francisco de Miranda. The illustration shows the basic tricolour before later national emblems were added.
nodes.imageCredit: Jorge Candeias / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Gran Colombia
nodes.note: Shared historical state behind the Colombian, Ecuadorian and Venezuelan branches; several variants existed. The illustration represents an 1821 variant.
nodes.imageCredit: Jaume Ollé / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Central American federation
nodes.note: Blue-white-blue federal flag. Dates include the United Provinces and Federal Republic periods. The illustration shows the federal republic variant used from 1824–1825.
nodes.imageCredit: Jaume Ollé / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Soviet Union
nodes.note: Red field with hammer, sickle and star. Minor construction changes are collapsed.
nodes.imageCredit: António Martins / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Byelorussian SSR
nodes.note: Red and green with a woven ornament, retained in altered form after Soviet symbols were removed.
nodes.imageCredit: Željko Heimer and Zachary Harden / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Socialist Yugoslavia
nodes.note: Blue-white-red with a red star, combining the Yugoslav tricolour with the emblem of the Partisan movement.
nodes.imageCredit: Željko Heimer / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Czechoslovakia
nodes.note: The Czech Republic retained this design after the federation dissolved. This same national flag continued under communist rule (1948–1989) and after the Velvet Revolution until dissolution in 1992.

nodes.name: German Empire
nodes.note: Black-white-red combines Prussian black-white with Hanseatic white-red. Hamburg’s modern castle flag exemplifies the latter heraldic tradition; black-red-gold belonged to a competing national tradition.
nodes.imageCredit: António Martins / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Weimar Republic
nodes.note: Black-red-gold returned to official use in 1919, drawing on the nineteenth-century liberal movement.
nodes.imageCredit: M. Schmöger / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: East Germany
nodes.note: The national emblem differentiated the GDR flag from the West German tricolour.
nodes.imageCredit: Jaume Ollé / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: South Africa, 1928
nodes.note: Orange-white-blue with three smaller flags, replaced at the end of apartheid.
nodes.imageCredit: Clay Moss / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Canadian Red Ensign
nodes.note: Representative late form of the ensign used before the Maple Leaf. Earlier arms variants are omitted.
nodes.imageCredit: Clay Moss / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Empire of Brazil
nodes.note: Green field and yellow diamond survived the change from monarchy to republic, while the central emblem changed.
nodes.imageCredit: Simon J. Frame, modified by Joseph McMillan / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Portugal, monarchy
nodes.note: Blue-white royal flag replaced by the republican red-green design; national arms continued in altered form.
nodes.imageCredit: António Martins / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Spanish Second Republic
nodes.note: Red-yellow-purple republican flag; the later state returned to red-yellow-red.
nodes.imageCredit: Luis Miguel Arias / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Libya, green flag
nodes.note: The plain green flag of Gaddafi’s state; replaced in 2011 by the restored independence design.
nodes.imageCredit: António Martins-Tuválkin / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Afghanistan, republic
nodes.note: Black-red-green republican tricolour, including later emblem variants as one design family. Its black-red-green tricolour was introduced in 1928 after Amanullah’s European journey, with the Weimar flag often cited as a model.

nodes.name: Myanmar, socialist design
nodes.note: Red with a blue canton containing the socialist emblem; replaced by the yellow-green-red triband in 2010. 5:9 variant. FOTW records adoption 27 December 1973 and constitution date 3 January 1974.
nodes.imageCredit: Željko Heimer / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Rwanda, R tricolour
nodes.note: Red-yellow-green with a central R, replaced in 2001 by a new blue-yellow-green design.
nodes.imageCredit: Željko Heimer / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Zaire
nodes.note: Green field with a yellow disc and torch, abandoned when the state again became the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Illustration shows the later 1990 specification of the same principal design.
nodes.imageCredit: Martin Grieve / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Georgia, 1990
nodes.note: Restored 1918 republic design; replaced by the five-cross flag in 2004.
nodes.imageCredit: Željko Heimer / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Lesotho, 1987
nodes.note: Diagonal design with military emblem, replaced by the triband and Basotho hat in 2006.
nodes.imageCredit: Željko Heimer / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Malawi, 2010
nodes.note: Brief redesign with a full white sun; the previous rising-sun design was restored in 2012.
nodes.imageCredit: Martin Grieve / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Tanganyika
nodes.note: Green-black-green with gold borders. Combined with Zanzibar’s colours in the Tanzanian flag.
nodes.imageCredit: Vincent Morley / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Zanzibar, 1964
nodes.note: Blue-black-green revolutionary colours, shown in the 1964 variant with a narrow white hoist stripe. These colours contributed to the new Tanzanian flag.
nodes.imageCredit: António Martins / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Eritrea, federation
nodes.note: Blue flag with a green olive wreath, an important emblem source for today’s flag. Federation-era Eritrean flag.
nodes.imageCredit: Mark Sensen and Dov Gutterman / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Trust Territory, Pacific
nodes.note: Blue field and six white stars representing island districts; predecessor administration of several Pacific states.
nodes.imageCredit: Phil Nelson / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Indian National Congress
nodes.note: Saffron-white-green with a spinning wheel; the national flag replaced the wheel with the Ashoka Chakra in 1947.
nodes.imageCredit: Dylan Crawfoot / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Bangladesh, 1971
nodes.note: Independence-war flag with a map inside the red disc; the map was removed in 1972.
nodes.imageCredit: Jorge Candeias / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Iran, Lion and Sun
nodes.note: Representative late monarchy flag. The 1980 redesign replaced the emblem and added border inscriptions. State flag with lion and sun. Source notes continued use until 1980.
nodes.imageCredit: Martin Grieve / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Korean Empire
nodes.note: Early Taegeukgi tradition, ancestral to the modern South Korean flag; exact trigram arrangements varied.
nodes.imageCredit: Kazutaka Nishiura / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Republic of China, mainland
nodes.note: The same principal design continues on Taiwan; the PRC adopted a different flag in 1949.

nodes.name: Nazi Germany
nodes.note: The swastika flag became the sole national flag in 1935, after being a co-national flag from 1933.
nodes.imageCredit: Mark Sensen and António Martins-Tuválkin / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Qing dynasty
nodes.note: Late rectangular yellow-dragon flag. Earlier imperial maritime flags were triangular.
nodes.imageCredit: Mario Fabretto / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: France, Bourbon Restoration
nodes.note: Plain white national flag under the restored Bourbon monarchy, interrupted during Napoleon’s Hundred Days in 1815. The tricolour returned in 1830.
nodes.imageCredit: Ivan Sache / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: China, five-colour republic
nodes.note: Five horizontal colours symbolised the early republic’s conception of its major peoples. Replaced by the Nationalist flag in 1928.
nodes.imageCredit: Miles Li / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Ottoman crescent & star
nodes.note: Ottoman crescent-and-star tradition, illustrated by its later five-pointed form. Star shapes varied; the often-quoted 1793 and 1844 standardisation dates are disputed.

nodes.name: Texas
nodes.note: The Lone Star flag began as the Republic of Texas national flag in 1839 and continued after statehood.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Ivan Sarajcic , 4 April 2007 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: California
nodes.note: The modern state flag revives the Bear Flag revolt of 1846; the bear was standardized in 1953.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Mario Fabretto , 24 February 1998 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Maryland
nodes.note: The quarters combine the Calvert and Crossland family arms.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Carlos Thompson , 8 July 2003 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: New Mexico
nodes.note: The Zia sun symbol appears in red on yellow; the colours recall Spain, while the emblem belongs to the Zia Pueblo tradition.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 16 March 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Ohio
nodes.note: John Eisenmann’s swallowtailed burgee has seventeen stars for statehood order and a disk suggesting the O of Ohio and a buckeye.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Zachary Harden , 19 May 2016 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Tennessee
nodes.note: Reeves’s 1905 design joins the three Grand Divisions in a blue circle. The museum distinguishes it from an unadopted Confederate-based proposal of 1861. Direct Confederate descent of this flag remains unsubstantiated.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 17 November 2006 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Alaska
nodes.note: Benny Benson’s design shows the Big Dipper and North Star, expressing Alaska’s northern setting.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Zachary Harden , 19 May 2016 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Colorado
nodes.note: Andrew Carlisle Carson’s red C frames a golden disk over blue and white stripes; specifications were refined in 1964.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 9 August 2007 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Arizona
nodes.note: Thirteen red and yellow rays recall the original states and the western sunset; the copper star reflects mining.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Zachary Harden , 19 May 2016 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Quebec
nodes.note: The Fleurdelisé combines a white cross with four upright fleurs-de-lis, drawing on French and French-Canadian traditions.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Martin Grieve The official proportions of the flag are: horizontally: 10-4-10 (=24) vertically: 6-4-6 (=16) with height of the fleur-de-lys: 4 The flag was officially confirmed on 21 January 1948 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: British Columbia
nodes.note: A banner of the provincial arms combines a Union flag with a setting sun and blue-white waves.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Martin Grieve and Christopher Southworth, 17-18 September 2005 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Ontario
nodes.note: A Red Ensign with the provincial shield retained the older Canadian ensign tradition after adoption of the Maple Leaf.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 21 August 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Manitoba
nodes.note: The Red Ensign carries the provincial shield with Saint George’s cross and a bison.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss, 17 August 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Nova Scotia
nodes.note: The banner of arms reverses Scotland’s white saltire on blue and adds the Scottish royal lion; its arms date to 1625.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 18 August 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: New South Wales
nodes.note: St George cross, stars and lion badge.
nodes.imageCredit: Clay Moss, 17 October 2008 / FOTW Flags Of The World

nodes.name: Victoria
nodes.note: Southern Cross and crown badge, introduced in 1877.
nodes.imageCredit: Martin Grieve, 26 January 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World

nodes.name: Queensland
nodes.note: Crowned Maltese cross badge.
nodes.imageCredit: Martin Grieve, 26 July 2008 / FOTW Flags Of The World

nodes.name: South Australia
nodes.note: Piping shrike badge on a golden disc.
nodes.imageCredit: Martin Grieve, 15 June 2006 / FOTW Flags Of The World

nodes.name: Western Australia
nodes.note: Black swan badge, confirmed in 1875. The swan was turned towards the hoist in 1953.
nodes.imageCredit: Martin Grieve, 1 March 2006 / FOTW Flags Of The World

nodes.name: Tasmania
nodes.note: Red lion badge on a white disc, used since 1876.
nodes.imageCredit: Martin Grieve, 27 November 2008 / FOTW Flags Of The World

nodes.name: Australian Capital Territory
nodes.note: Adopted in 1993. The Southern Cross accompanies a modified version of Canberra’s arms in the territory’s blue and gold colours.
nodes.imageCredit: Martin Grieve, 14 June 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World

nodes.name: Northern Territory
nodes.note: Robert Ingpen’s 1978 design combines the Southern Cross with a Sturt’s desert rose in black, white and ochre.
nodes.imageCredit: Martin Grieve, 27 April 2006 / FOTW Flags Of The World

nodes.name: Basque Country
nodes.note: The Arana brothers introduced the Ikurrina in 1894 for Biscay. Its red field, green saltire and white cross drew on Biscay’s symbolism; it became the Basque government flag in 1936.
nodes.imageCredit: António Martins-Tuválkin, 14 December 2023 / FOTW Flags Of The World

nodes.name: Catalonia · Senyera
nodes.note: Four red bars on gold derive from the medieval royal arms shared by the Crown of Aragon and the House of Barcelona. The plain Senyera serves as Catalonia’s flag.
nodes.imageCredit: António Martins, 28 October 2017 / FOTW Flags Of The World

nodes.name: Aragon
nodes.note: The regional flag combines the four red bars on gold with Aragon’s coat of arms. Its current regulation dates from 1984.
nodes.imageCredit: Antonio Gutiérrez / S.E.V., 24 September 1999 / FOTW Flags Of The World

nodes.name: Valencian Community
nodes.note: The crowned Senyera adds a decorated blue band to the four red bars on gold. Its medieval Valencian tradition was recognised in the 1982 Statute of Autonomy.
nodes.imageCredit: Jaume Ollé / FOTW Flags Of The World

nodes.name: Brittany
nodes.note: Morvan Marchal combined Breton ermine and nine black-and-white stripes in 1923. The stripes represent Brittany’s traditional dioceses.
nodes.imageCredit: Vincent Morley, 6 July 2000 / FOTW Flags Of The World

nodes.name: Bavaria · lozenges
nodes.note: The white-blue lozenges continue the Wittelsbach dynastic tradition; Bavaria also has an equally official striped flag.
nodes.imageCredit: M. Schmöger / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Majapahit · attributed banner
nodes.note: Modern reconstruction traditionally attributed to the Majapahit Empire (1293–c.1527). The exact historical flag design is disputed. Nine red-and-white stripes also appear in Indonesia’s modern naval jack. Alleged borrowing by the English East India Company remains unconfirmed.
nodes.imageCredit: Mark Sensen, 21 May 1998 / FOTW Flags Of The World

nodes.name: Indonesia · naval jack
nodes.note: Nine alternating red and white stripes. Flags of the World records the traditional attribution of this design to Majapahit.
nodes.imageCredit: Mark Sensen, 21 May 1998 / FOTW Flags Of The World

nodes.name: California · Bear Flag
nodes.note: William Todd’s Bear Flag, one of several designs used during the 1846 revolt. This illustration reconstructs the Todd example, destroyed in the 1906 San Francisco fire.
nodes.imageCredit: Pete Loeser, 20 July 2014, after James J. Ferrigan III / FOTW Flags Of The World

nodes.name: Texas · Burnet flag
nodes.note: Blue with a gold star: the Republic of Texas national standard adopted in December 1836. Replaced as the national flag in 1839; it continued as the war flag until 1845.
nodes.imageCredit: Chris Pinette, 29 April 1997 / FOTW Flags Of The World

nodes.name: Mississippi
nodes.note: The magnolia design approved by voters in 2020 became official in 2021, replacing the flag bearing a Confederate battle emblem.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 15 November 2020 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Mississippi · former flag
nodes.note: The state flag adopted in 1894 incorporated the Confederate battle emblem. The legislature retired it in 2020. This illustration shows the later standard version with a white border around the canton.
nodes.imageCredit: Clay Moss, 28 December 2005 / FOTW Flags Of The World

nodes.name: Confederate battle flag
nodes.note: Southern Cross battle design introduced in 1861. Shown: the square Army of Northern Virginia pattern of 1863, with thirteen stars and white outer border. Confederate units used several variants.
nodes.imageCredit: Rick Wyatt, 20 November 1997 / FOTW Flags Of The World

nodes.name: Brittany · ducal ermine banner
nodes.note: Modern rendering of the ducal arms as a banner: an ermine field. The arms are recorded on a seal of 1318.
nodes.imageCredit: Mikael Bodlore-Penlaez / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Brittany · Kroaz Du
nodes.note: Black-cross flag used in medieval Brittany. The date gives an approximate period; the early chronology remains uncertain.
nodes.imageCredit: Ivan Sache / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Belgrano · early flag reconstruction
nodes.note: Reconstruction of an early Belgrano flag associated with 1813. The precise arrangement first raised in 1812 is uncertain; its colours came from the revolutionary cockade.
nodes.imageCredit: Jaume Ollé / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Cyrenaica · Senussi black flag
nodes.note: Black flag with white crescent and star associated with the Sanusiyya and Emir Idris. Attested for postwar Cyrenaica; projecting this exact design back to the nineteenth century or 1919 lacks evidence.
nodes.imageCredit: Ivan Sache / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Revolutionary red banner
nodes.note: The red banner became a socialist emblem in the 1848 revolutions and was used by the Paris Commune in 1871. Russian and later communist movements adopted this political colour tradition.
nodes.imageCredit: Ivan Sache / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Abbasid black · dynastic colour
nodes.note: Black was associated with the Abbasids and is recalled in Pan-Arab symbolism. The plain field is a schematic illustration of the dynastic colour.
nodes.imageCredit: Syed Junaid Imam / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Umayyad white · dynastic attribution
nodes.note: Schematic illustration of the white assigned to the Umayyads in modern Pan-Arab interpretation.
nodes.imageCredit: Syed Junaid Imam / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Fatimid green · later attribution
nodes.note: Modern Pan-Arab accounts assign green to the Fatimids; historical scholarship identifies their dynastic colour as white. This schematic illustrates the later attribution.
nodes.imageCredit: António Martins-Tuválkin / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Hashemite red · dynastic colour
nodes.note: The Royal Hashemite Court traces a dark-red banner to Sharif Abu Nami (1515–1520) and the initial Arab Revolt. The illustration represents the colour schematically.
nodes.imageCredit: Ivan Sache / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Arab Literature Club · reported flag
nodes.note: Reported white-black-green-red flag used in 1909–1911. The source explains its colours through Safi al-Din al-Hilli’s medieval poem about deeds, battles, fields and swords.
nodes.imageCredit: Ivan Sache / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Young Arab movement · reported flag
nodes.note: Reported green-white-black flag associated with the Young Arab movement and Ottoman Decentralization Party, preceding the Arab Revolt design.
nodes.imageCredit: Ivan Sache / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Federation of Malaya · 1950
nodes.note: Eleven stripes and an eleven-pointed star represented the original federation. The design expanded to fourteen stripes and points when Malaysia formed in 1963. Proposed Majapahit ancestry remains uncertain.
nodes.imageCredit: Clay Moss / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Johor
nodes.note: Johor’s blue flag with a red crescent-and-star canton. A reported design influence on Mohamed Hamzah’s winning Malayan proposal.
nodes.imageCredit: Image located by Hashimi / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Malawi · independence flag
nodes.note: Original rising-sun flag, used from independence until the 2010 redesign. Restored in 2012.

nodes.name: Libya · independence flag
nodes.note: Independence design combining Cyrenaica’s black crescent-and-star flag with red and green. Restored in 2011.

nodes.name: Libya · Arab Republic
nodes.note: Plain red-white-black flag introduced after the 1969 overthrow of the monarchy.
nodes.imageCredit: Santiago Dotor / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Germany · 1848 tricolour
nodes.note: Black-red-gold of the liberal national movement, officially adopted in 1848. Accounts of the colours emphasize student associations and the Lützow volunteers.
nodes.imageCredit: M. Schmöger / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Alabama
nodes.note: A crimson Saint Andrew’s cross on white, adopted in 1895. A Confederate origin is debated.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Joe McMillan , 23 February 2000 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Arkansas
nodes.note: The diamond recalls Arkansas’s diamond deposits; 25 border stars mark statehood order, while an interior star commemorates the Confederacy.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Zachary Harden , 31 July 2018 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Connecticut
nodes.note: The three grapevines and motto derive from the colonial seal tradition.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 1 February 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Delaware
nodes.note: The state arms stand inside a buff diamond; the date records ratification of the United States Constitution.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 19 February 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Florida
nodes.note: The red saltire was added in 1900; the central state seal was corrected in 1985.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 28 January 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Georgia
nodes.note: The three stripes and star-ringed canton recall the Confederate first national flag; the canton contains Georgia’s arms and motto.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 13 December 2014 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Idaho
nodes.note: The state seal and name appear on blue, continuing the military-colour pattern used by many states.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 29 January 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Illinois
nodes.note: The 1915 white flag with the state seal was revised in 1970 to include the state’s name.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 14 March 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Indiana
nodes.note: Paul Hadley’s torch represents liberty and enlightenment; nineteen stars mark Indiana’s admission order.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 24 October 2007 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Iowa
nodes.note: Dixie Cornell Gebhardt’s blue-white-red tricolour recalls the territory’s French history; an eagle carries the state motto.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Mario Fabretto , 24 February 1998 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Kansas
nodes.note: The state seal and sunflower crest appear on blue; the name Kansas was added in 1961.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 30 January 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Kentucky
nodes.note: The seal shows two figures clasping hands under the state name and above goldenrod sprigs.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 2 February 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Louisiana
nodes.note: The pelican feeding its young is an old state emblem. The current artwork restores three drops of blood required by the 2006 law.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 9 December 2011 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Maine
nodes.note: The state arms on blue replaced the 1901 pine-tree-and-star flag.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Dave Martucci , 6 September 1996 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Massachusetts
nodes.note: The state arms appear on white; since 1971 the same design appears on both sides.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Mario Fabretto , 24 February 1998 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Michigan
nodes.note: The blue flag carries the state arms, with elk and moose supporters and the motto about seeking a pleasant peninsula.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 8 February 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Minnesota
nodes.note: A North Star and a dark-blue shape suggesting Minnesota meet a light-blue field. This replaced the seal flag in May 2024.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Tomislav Todorovic , 31 December 2023 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Missouri
nodes.note: Missouri has retained Marie Elizabeth Watkins Oliver’s 1913 design: American colours, the state arms, and 24 stars. The historical original and modern illustrations represent the same principal design.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 24 October 2007 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Montana
nodes.note: The state seal appears on blue; Montana was added above it in 1981.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 4 November 2014 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Nebraska
nodes.note: The state seal appears in gold and silver on a blue field; the 1925 banner was designated a flag in 1963.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 4 February 2008 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Nevada
nodes.note: The silver star, sagebrush and Battle Born scroll occupy the canton. The name’s placement was revised in 1991.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 28 March 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: New Hampshire
nodes.note: The state seal with the frigate Raleigh is surrounded by laurel and nine stars; the seal was revised in 1931.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 4 February 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: New Jersey
nodes.note: The state arms appear on buff. The colours recall New Jersey’s Revolutionary-era military uniform tradition.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 22 February 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: New York
nodes.note: The state arms appear on blue; E Pluribus Unum was added beneath Excelsior in 2020.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Jean-Marc Merklin , 18 January 2025 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: North Carolina
nodes.note: The 1885 revision exchanged the 1861 flag’s red and blue fields and replaced the secession date with the Halifax Resolves date.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Blas Delgado Ortiz and António Martins-Tuválkin , 27 January 2002 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: North Dakota
nodes.note: The design follows the North Dakota infantry regimental colour used in the Spanish-American War, adding the state name.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Zachary Harden , 26 May 2016 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Oklahoma
nodes.note: An Osage buffalo-hide shield is crossed by a peace pipe and olive branch. The state name was added in 1941.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Charlotte Zakharian Jones , 18 November 2005 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Oregon
nodes.note: The obverse carries the state seal, name and admission year; the reverse uniquely shows a beaver.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 16 March 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Pennsylvania
nodes.note: The state coat of arms appears on a blue field, standardized in 1907.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 11 March 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Rhode Island
nodes.note: An anchor and Hope motto continue colonial symbolism; thirteen stars recall the original states.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Mario Fabretto , 24 February 1998 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: South Carolina
nodes.note: The palmetto and crescent continue Revolutionary-era symbolism associated with the defence of Sullivan’s Island.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Mario Fabretto , 24 February 1998 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: South Dakota
nodes.note: The seal sits inside the rays of the earlier sun flag; the inscription changed to The Mount Rushmore State in 1992.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 16 February 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Utah
nodes.note: A new beehive flag replaced the seal design in March 2024; the former flag retains official historic status.
nodes.imageCredit: image located by Dave Fowler , 11 November 2022 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Vermont
nodes.note: The state arms on blue replaced an earlier design resembling the United States flag.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 11 February 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Virginia
nodes.note: The state seal depicts Virtue over fallen Tyranny, continuing imagery developed during the Revolution.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Mario Fabretto , 24 February 1998 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Washington
nodes.note: The green field carries the state seal with George Washington’s portrait; the seal’s appearance was standardized in 1967.
nodes.imageCredit: image located by António Martins-Tuválkin , 4 April 2018 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: West Virginia
nodes.note: The state arms and rhododendron wreath appear on white with a blue border.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Mario Fabretto , 24 February 1998 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Wisconsin
nodes.note: The arms on blue were supplemented by the state name and 1848; the 1979 amendment took full effect in 1981.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 28 February 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Wyoming
nodes.note: Verna Keays’s design places the state seal on a white bison inside a blue field with white and red borders.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 23 February 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Alberta
nodes.note: The provincial shield appears on blue: Saint George’s cross above mountains, prairie and wheat.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss , 16 August 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: New Brunswick
nodes.note: A banner of the provincial arms combines a lion with a ship, recalling heraldic and maritime traditions.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss, 15 August 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Newfoundland and Labrador
nodes.note: Christopher Pratt’s flag uses blue triangles that recall the Union flag, with white, red and gold forms expressing the province’s identity.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss, 19 August 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Northwest Territories
nodes.note: Robert Bessant’s blue-white-blue design places the territorial shield on a broad central Canadian pale.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss, 14 August 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Nunavut
nodes.note: A red inuksuk and blue North Star express Inuit navigation and guidance; the flag was introduced with the territory in 1999.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Arnaud Leroy, 1 April 1999 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Prince Edward Island
nodes.note: A banner of the provincial arms shows the royal lion and trees symbolizing the island and its three counties.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss, 20 August 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Saskatchewan
nodes.note: Green and gold evoke forest and grain fields; the shield and western red lily add provincial emblems.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss, 22 August 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Yukon
nodes.note: Lynn Lambert’s green-white-blue flag carries the territorial arms above fireweed.
nodes.imageCredit: image by Clay Moss, 22 August 2009 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Baden-Württemberg
nodes.note: The official flag places the state arms on black and gold. Its shield assembles the heraldic traditions of the merged territories.
nodes.imageCredit: M. Schmöger / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Berlin
nodes.note: A black bear appears on white between red stripes, continuing the city’s heraldic emblem.
nodes.imageCredit: M. Schmöger / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Brandenburg
nodes.note: The red eagle of Brandenburg appears on the red-white state flag, reviving historic regional heraldry.
nodes.imageCredit: M. Schmöger / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Bremen
nodes.note: The striped and checked red-white flag belongs to the Hanseatic colour tradition; this is the civil variant without arms.
nodes.imageCredit: M. Schmöger / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Hamburg
nodes.note: The white castle on red develops the city’s medieval seal and Hanseatic colours. Readopted in 1952; the flag tradition is earlier.
nodes.imageCredit: M. Schmöger / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Hesse
nodes.note: The red-white striped lion in the state arms continues the heraldic tradition shared with medieval Thuringia.
nodes.imageCredit: M. Schmöger / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania
nodes.note: The official flag combines Mecklenburg’s bull and Pomerania’s griffin with colours associated with the component territories.
nodes.imageCredit: M. Schmöger / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Lower Saxony
nodes.note: The white Saxon horse is placed on the German black-red-gold tricolour.
nodes.imageCredit: M. Schmöger / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: North Rhine-Westphalia
nodes.note: The official flag combines Rhine, Westphalian horse and Lippe rose arms over green, white and red.
nodes.imageCredit: M. Schmöger / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Rhineland-Palatinate
nodes.note: Germany’s black-red-gold carries a shield with Trier’s cross, Mainz’s wheel and the Palatinate lion.
nodes.imageCredit: M. Schmöger / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Saarland
nodes.note: The German tricolour carries a shield combining the historic arms of territories within the Saarland.
nodes.imageCredit: M. Schmöger / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Saxony
nodes.note: The official state flag adds Saxony’s black-gold shield and green crancelin to the white-green bicolour, whose colours date to 1815.
nodes.imageCredit: M. Schmöger / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Saxony-Anhalt
nodes.note: The yellow-black official flag carries a shield combining Saxon and Anhalt heraldry..
nodes.imageCredit: M. Schmöger / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Schleswig-Holstein
nodes.note: The official flag adds Schleswig’s lions and Holstein’s nettle leaf to the blue-white-red regional tricolour.
nodes.imageCredit: M. Schmöger / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Thuringia
nodes.note: The official state flag adds the striped lion and eight stars to a white-red bicolour.
nodes.imageCredit: M. Schmöger / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Minnesota · seal flag
nodes.note: The 1983 seal revision on medium blue preceded the North Star redesign of 2024.
nodes.imageCredit: Tomislav Todorovic, 5 October 2025 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Utah · seal flag
nodes.note: The corrected 2011 seal flag was replaced as the primary state flag in 2024 and retained as the historic state flag.
nodes.imageCredit: Pete Loeser, 9 April 2012 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Louisiana · earlier pelican flag
nodes.note: An earlier rendering of the pelican flag without the restored three blood drops; the state updated the artwork in 2010.
nodes.imageCredit: Clay Moss, 23 December 2006 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Louisiana · 1861 flag
nodes.note: Louisiana’s Confederate-era state flag adapted the American canton-and-thirteen-stripes layout using French colours and a red canton with a gold star.
nodes.imageCredit: António Martins-Tuválkin, 10 August 2007 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Texas · naval ensign
nodes.note: The Republic of Texas naval ensign adapted the U.S. flag’s thirteen stripes and blue canton, substituting a single white star.
nodes.imageCredit: Ivan Sarajčić and António Martins-Tuválkin, 21 June 2025 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Confederacy · Stars and Bars
nodes.note: The first Confederate national flag used a blue star canton and red-white-red bars. This seven-star version dates from 1861; later versions added stars. It is distinct from the saltire battle flag.
nodes.imageCredit: Clay Moss, 2 November 2007 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Prussia · black and white
nodes.note: The black-white civil flag represents Prussian heraldic livery colours, taken from the black eagle on white. Those colours helped form the later German black-white-red tricolour.
nodes.imageCredit: Jaume Ollé / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Kenya African National Union
nodes.note: The black-red-green party palette preceded Kenya’s flag. Reports describe variants with rooster, shield and weapon emblems; the illustration represents the party design.
nodes.imageCredit: Jorge Candeias / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Kenya African Union
nodes.note: Predecessor organization of KANU, using a black-red-green flag with a shield and weapons.
nodes.imageCredit: Ivan Sache / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Malawi Congress Party · plain triband
nodes.note: The party’s black-red-green triband underlies Malawi’s independence flag. This is the documented plain variant; other party versions include a rooster. The year marks the party’s formation.
nodes.imageCredit: Jarig Bakker / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: MPLA · red-black flag
nodes.note: Red over black with a central yellow star. This party design was the principal model for independent Angola’s flag.
nodes.imageCredit: António Martins / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: FRELIMO · original flag
nodes.note: The earlier striped FRELIMO flag, with white divisions and a red hoist triangle. The date marks the movement’s founding; this is distinct from later red party flags.
nodes.imageCredit: António Martins / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: SWAPO · liberation flag
nodes.note: Blue-red-green horizontal tricolour used by SWAPO during the liberation struggle; its colours contributed to Namibia’s national flag.
nodes.imageCredit: Jorge Candeias and Tomislav Todorović / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: PAIGC
nodes.note: Shared liberation-party design behind Guinea-Bissau’s flag and Cape Verde’s original flag. The illustrated party version includes initials; forms and proportions vary.
nodes.imageCredit: Jorge Candeias / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Cape Verde · independence flag
nodes.note: National flag used from independence in 1975 until replacement in 1992; shared PAIGC origins with Guinea-Bissau’s flag.
nodes.imageCredit: Orange Tuesday and António Martins / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Gulf · maritime red tradition
nodes.note: Plain red flags preceded the differentiated flags of several Gulf coastal states. A historical Bahrain flag illustrates this regional colour tradition.
nodes.imageCredit: Santiago Dotor / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Syria · independence flag
nodes.note: Green-white-black independence design with three red stars, also restored in 1961–1963. The current flag revives this tradition.

nodes.name: Benin · People’s Republic
nodes.note: Green with a revolutionary red star, used under the People’s Republic. The independence flag returned in 1990.
nodes.imageCredit: Željko Heimer (2001) / FOTW Flags Of The World

nodes.name: Congo · People’s Republic
nodes.note: Red socialist flag with the party-inspired emblem. Adopted at the end of 1969 and used from January 1970.
nodes.imageCredit: Željko Heimer (2001) / FOTW Flags Of The World

nodes.name: Russian SFSR · 1918
nodes.note: Early Russian Soviet flag with ornamental Cyrillic initials, approved in May 1918.
nodes.imageCredit: António Martins (2002) / FOTW Flags Of The World

nodes.name: Russian SFSR · 1954
nodes.note: Soviet red, hammer and sickle, with a blue hoist stripe identifying the Russian republic.
nodes.imageCredit: António Martins (2003) / FOTW Flags Of The World

nodes.name: NLF / Republic of South Vietnam
nodes.note: Red-blue revolutionary flag used by the National Liberation Front and the Provisional Revolutionary Government of South Vietnam. Designs varied; the illustrated version is associated with the 1969 government.
nodes.imageCredit: Jaume Ollé / FOTW Flags Of The World

nodes.name: Benin · independence flag
nodes.note: Independence design, later restored after the socialist period.

nodes.name: Republic of the Congo · independence flag
nodes.note: Independence design, later restored after the socialist period.

nodes.name: Quebec · Carillon
nodes.note: Elphège Filiatrault’s Carillon flag placed four fleurs-de-lis pointing towards a white cross on blue. The 1948 flag straightened the fleurs-de-lis.
nodes.imageCredit: Olivier Touzeau, 7 June 2020 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Kingdom of Yugoslavia
nodes.note: Blue-white-red national tricolour of the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, renamed Yugoslavia in 1929. The uncharged national form is shown.
nodes.imageCredit: Željko Heimer, 16 November 2003 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Kazakh SSR
nodes.note: Late Soviet republican flag, retained briefly after independence before the 1992 redesign.
nodes.imageCredit: António Martins, 30 October 2002 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Kirghiz SSR
nodes.note: Late Soviet republican flag, replaced by the sun-and-tunduk design in 1992.
nodes.imageCredit: Željko Heimer, 6 May 2000 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Uzbek SSR
nodes.note: Late Soviet republican flag, replaced by independent Uzbekistan’s tricolour.
nodes.imageCredit: António Martins, 28 October 2002 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Turkmen SSR
nodes.note: Late Soviet republican flag, replaced by Turkmenistan’s green carpet-emblem design.
nodes.imageCredit: António Martins, 28 December 2002 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Tajik SSR
nodes.note: The white and green bands carried agricultural meanings. Independent Tajikistan retained these colours in its new arrangement.
nodes.imageCredit: Željko Heimer, 17 April 1996 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Cross of Burgundy
nodes.note: Ragged red saltire associated with the Burgundian dynasty and Spanish military flags from the sixteenth century. The white-field form is shown.
nodes.imageCredit: Sergio Camero; GIF by Santiago Dotor / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: France · blue cross ensign
nodes.note: Pre-revolutionary French civil ensign: a white cross on blue. Several related forms coexisted; the date indicates an approximate period.
nodes.imageCredit: Pierre Gay, 29 September 1998 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: East Turkestan · Kök Bayraq
nodes.note: Blue crescent-and-star flag used by the modern East Turkestan movement. Its precise use by the 1933 republic is disputed; early coin depictions show other forms.
nodes.imageCredit: Željko Heimer and António Martins-Tuválkin, 9 December 2007 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: All-India Muslim League
nodes.note: Green crescent-and-star movement flag, retained by later Muslim League parties. Pakistan’s national flag added a white hoist band.
nodes.imageCredit: FOTW contributors; page text by Glen Robert-Grant Hodgins, 19 May 1998; image author unspecified / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: France · royal white ensign
nodes.note: Plain white naval ensign of the Bourbon monarchy. Royal white also contributed to the revolutionary tricolour.
nodes.imageCredit: Ivan Sache / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Slovak plain tricolour
nodes.note: White-blue-red became the established order after earlier Slovak red-white and pan-Slavic variants of 1848. European revolutionary tricolours provided a wider political context; the cited national histories document local heraldic and Pan-Slavic colour sources.

nodes.name: Liberty League · 1917

nodes.name: Army of the Three Guarantees

nodes.name: Serbian plain tricolour

nodes.name: Slovene tricolour · 1848

nodes.name: North Carolina · 1861

nodes.name: Bohemia / Czechoslovakia

nodes.name: Croatian tricolour · 1848
nodes.note: The red-white-blue tricolour became a Croatian national symbol in 1848, alongside heraldic versions. Its colours came from Croatian, Slavonian and Dalmatian heraldry, within the wider revolutionary and Pan-Slavic setting.

nodes.name: Islamic crescent tradition
nodes.note: Ottoman prestige helped make the crescent a widely recognised Islamic emblem. Its earlier history includes Persian, Byzantine and Central Asian uses; the ultimate route is disputed.

nodes.name: Russia
nodes.note: Russia restored its white-blue-red tricolour in 1991, replacing the Russian SFSR flag. The design has seventeenth-century origins.

nodes.name: Castile, castle banner (modern rendering)
nodes.imageCredit: Antonio Gutiérrez and Ignacio Munguía / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/
nodes.note: Modern regionalist rendition of the Castilian golden castle on red, illustrating the medieval heraldic motif. The date gives its approximate medieval context.

nodes.name: France · fleurs-de-lis banner
nodes.note: Blue strewn with golden fleurs-de-lis was used in medieval French royal heraldry. The illustrated banner represents this heraldic design.
nodes.imageCredit: Pierre Gay / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: France · three fleurs-de-lis
nodes.note: The French royal arms were simplified to three golden fleurs-de-lis in the 14th century. The illustration is a modern rendering of the banner of arms.
nodes.imageCredit: Rick Wyatt / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Bulgaria · plain tricolour
nodes.note: The 1879 constitution specifies white, green and red horizontal bands; the 1947 constitution adds the arms. The illustration uses modern proportions and shades to represent the plain motif, which continued as a civil ensign after 1947.
nodes.imageCredit: Zoltan Horvath, 24 April 2024 / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.name: Qajar Iran · Lion and Sun state ensign
nodes.note: State ensign documented in the 1910 Admiralty and 1917 National Geographic flag books, with pale colours. The dates identify the documented example and the Qajar dynasty’s end in 1925. The plain civil tricolour is recorded separately from 1906.
nodes.imageCredit: Željko Heimer / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.note: Vertical black-red-green tricolour with a mountain-and-sun emblem, introduced after Amanullah’s European tour. Sources date its introduction between June and September 1928 and describe different emblem colours. Encyclopaedia Iranica places its form in the European tricolour tradition.

nodes.note: Red-black-white vertical tricolour attributed to Habibullah Ghazi (Kalakani), January–October 1929, following Baert 2001. Accounts differ: Encyclopaedia Iranica describes the restoration of the earlier black national flag during his rule.
nodes.imageCredit: Ivan Sache / FOTW Flags Of The World website at https://www.fotw.info/

nodes.note: Introduced in 1996. Green represents prosperity, white peace, red the liberation struggle, and the shahada Islam. A reported source is the Somali National Movement flag, with its colours rearranged. Its palette also appears in Pan-Arab flags.

nodes.name: Somaliland · first republic flag

scope: All 193 UN member states and both observer states; selected disputed states, associated states and constituent nations; influential historical and movement flags. Historical coverage is selective.
methodology: Relationships distinguish documented influence, uncertain influence, redesign or succession, shared tradition, and visual resemblance. Dates identify the principal design or represented historical period. Arrows describe descent; horizontal groups show related designs.

traditions.name: Saxon heraldry

traditions.name: Turkic sky colours
traditions.description: Blue expresses sky and Turkic identity in several flags; green also expresses religion, landscape and renewal, with meanings differing by state.

traditions.name: Tricolours of 1848
traditions.description: National tricolours adopted during and after the 1848 revolutions, using local heraldic colours and Pan-Slavic associations.

traditions.name: Imperial double eagles
traditions.description: Double-headed eagles served different imperial and dynastic traditions, with several disputed routes of transmission.

traditions.name: National birds
traditions.description: Uganda’s grey crowned crane, Zambia’s fish eagle and Zimbabwe’s stone bird identify national histories and emblems.

traditions.name: Yugoslav republics
traditions.description: The socialist republic flags combined local colours or arms with Yugoslav communist symbolism.

traditions.name: Pan-African colour traditions
traditions.description: Ethiopian green-yellow-red, ANC black-green-gold and Garvey red-black-green became overlapping political colour traditions. A single line of borrowing between these three flags is unestablished.

traditions.name: Slavic national tricolours
traditions.description: White, blue and red national tricolours developed through Russian associations and existing local heraldry.

traditions.name: Pan-Arab colours
traditions.description: Black, white, red and green recur in Arab and neighbouring Islamic flag traditions; Somaliland uses this palette with local meanings.

traditions.name: Soviet republics
traditions.description: The fifteen late-Soviet union republic flags adapt the red field and communist emblems. Their national successors appear below.

traditions.name: Pan-African palettes
traditions.description: Jamaica, Guyana and Grenada share colours associated with African-diaspora and Pan-African identity. Each flag also assigns local meanings to its colours.

traditions.name: Latin American independence
traditions.description: The Miranda and Belgrano designs anchor two major independence-era flag lineages.

traditions.name: Red saltires
traditions.description: Alabama and Florida share a red saltire on white; the source histories discuss their separate adoptions.

traditions.name: Regional red and white
traditions.description: Indonesia and Singapore share a red-over-white field. Singapore’s designer explicitly considered Indonesia’s flag when distinguishing Singapore’s design.

traditions.name: Unity & revolution
traditions.description: Cameroon’s star represents national unity; Senegal’s unity and hope; Burkina Faso’s the guidance of the revolution.

traditions.name: Southern Cross
traditions.description: Both flags use the Southern Cross. Papua New Guinea’s constellation expresses links with Australia and the South Pacific.
